note: BUMPED to 1.0.6 from 1.0.5. THE TRANSCRIPTION IS UNCHANGED: source.txt is byte-identical to 1.0.5’s (sha256 748e58cef10981193585a101fcf67951cc3a37577eaf756f08399e343e1dd8bf) and the division model is CARRIED UNCHANGED (divisions.json byte-identical), because this bump is about RULES, EVIDENCE AND ONE INSTRUMENT and nothing else. WHAT 1.0.5 SERVED THAT THE PRINT DOES NOT CARRY, and this version closes. 1.0.5’s print-error-emendation class — the ONLY class that says the print’s own form is at fault — rested on two signals that were not measurements of the print: W asked only whether a changed word is absent from the REFERENCE WORDLIST, R only whether the print uses the form rarely. So r9734 mapped `consubsistS` to `consubsist` on a dictionary miss, while the print reads `consubsists` (1×, plus its own `consubsistent` 32×) and the rule’s target `consubsist` occurs NOWHERE in the print at all — the rule dropped the verb’s final s, the same defect shape 1.0.5 had removed from the contradiction class. r10277 mapped `, rythm a` to `, rhythm a` on a dictionary miss, while `rythm` is the print’s DOMINANT spelling (4× + rythms 1× against rhythm 2× + rhythms 1×): a modernisation of the print’s own orthography, not the repair of a misprint. And r8627’s `prophesy` -> `prophecy` fired on a 1×-vs-1× TIE (prophesy 1×, prophecy 1×). THE POSITIVE TEST, now required for that class: the print’s own form at the point is NOT a word of the reference wordlist, AND the print uses it NOWHERE ELSE in its own text (≤1× in both volumes together), AND the rule’s target IS what the print reads elsewhere, used MORE OFTEN. MEASURED over 1.0.5’s six: it licenses r10212 (`recal` 1× -> `recall` 8×), r10469 (`poeonian` 1× -> `pæonian` 3×) and r10931 (`gorgies` 1× -> `gorgias` 20×), and it refuses r8627, r10277 and r9734. A tie now has its own class, `indeterminate-tie`, whose action is to KEEP the flag, because a 1×-vs-1× tie from a re-flowed witness settles neither direction. RE-ADJUDICATED, by the mechanism that is honest for each: r9734’s target is CORRECTED to the print’s own `consubsists` as a NEW id (r11856) with r9734 retired — the transcription’s `consubsistS` is the print’s word with its final s mis-cased, so the rule does real work and only its TARGET was wrong; withdrawing it would have served the raw case damage. r10277 is WITHDRAWN, so the edition now serves `rythm`. r8627 keeps its flag with the tie stated as the reason. The version carries 3,262 rules against 1.0.5’s 3,263. THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG IN TWO PLACES AND IS CORRECTED, EACH WITH ITS NUMBERS. (1) The whole-reading test demanded the witness carry the rule’s `after` TOKEN RUN AS WRITTEN, including two things the witness’s own record says it does not model — this transcription’s apparatus token (`@`, a footnote asterisk) and a printed PAGE NUMBER, ours or PG’s inline one. A test that requires the witness to carry what the tool itself declares it cannot carry measures our apparatus, not the print. The test now also runs on the reading’s WORDS (the exact run is tried first, so this can only ADD confirmations), guarded so that it applies only where the rule’s change ADDS A WORD and the rule is not typed punctuation; MEASURED, that confirms SEVEN rules (r8576 r8594 r8998 r9122 r9270 r9542 r10219) and one more (r10517) that had been held as NO EVIDENCE, and it changes 8 decisions in total with ZERO placement changes and ZERO changes to the punctuation surface. ALL EIGHT are flag changes: no reading the edition serves moves. (2) The record’s own account of the 8 rules 1.0.5 re-flagged said they differ from the witness “in PAGE NUMBERS or in marks” — TRUE for seven of the ten in that class and FALSE for two: r10558 (`d has a` vs `and has a`) and r11093 (`t is e` vs `it is evidently`) differ by a PAGE-BREAK WORD FRAGMENT, and their real fix is a WIDER rule re-joined to whole words under a new id, which this unit records as a separate job rather than pretending the flag is about numbers. AND THE GUARD THAT POLICES CLEARS AND RE-FLAGS IS NO LONGER VACUOUSLY SATISFIABLE: a clear must now gain evidence whose GAINED entry carries its OWN justification (it could previously pass on an OLD entry’s), a re-flag must move its evidence WITHOUT SHRINKING it (deleting all evidence previously counted as movement) and must GROW its rationale with a stated marker. Each of the three was proven by asymmetry against the previous revision of the gate. WHAT IS NOT DONE, STATED: the two page-break fragments above; and the taxonomy gap 1.0.5 recorded is unchanged (a rule is still typed `OCR` where the transcription already reads the print).
